correctness.rationale: The positional expansions have valid digits for b>=7 and exact sums b-2 and b, giving equality. The squarefree equivalence follows from gcd(b,2b-3)=gcd(b,3) and gcd(b-2,2b-3)=1. Local prime-square restrictions are 1/2 at 2, 5/9 at 3, and 1-3/p^2 for every p>=5. Chinese remainder densities converge to the stated Euler product; the omitted large-prime-square contribution is bounded by 3T sum_{p>P}(1/p^2)+3 sqrt(2T), proving existence, value, and positivity of the limit. The standalone verifier confirms digit sums for 29,994 bases, squarefree equivalence for 1,994 bases, and 11 local prime counts; finite tests are not a proof.

originality.rationale: Primary full-text comparison: the 2023 paper poses the universal squarefree digit-sum collision question (Question 30), proves only unrestricted-base collisions in Example 11, and lists squarefree b<=10 examples in Example 14. The b=7 example exactly matches the new witness family and is acknowledged; the quantified family for infinitely many b>=11 and its exact positive-density Euler product are not stated or implied in the inspected primary text. Targeted literature and mathematical-record searches identified no dominating result. This is a best-knowledge originality assessment, not a proof of uniqueness.
residual_risks: The b=7 specialization is explicitly known from the source: some algebraic interpolation from that example is possible.
Independent papers, unpublished notes, and unindexed later solutions may already state the infinite-family construction or a broader theorem.
The source paper does not state that the universal b>=11 problem is still open in 2026; no such open-status claim is made.
Other sections and appendices of the public source were not reviewed line by line; the directly relevant examples and problem statement were read in full.

value.rationale: The primary paper explicitly asks whether H_b(n)=nS_b(n) is noninjective on squarefree inputs for all b>=11. Producing a uniform explicit squarefree witness on an infinite set of bases of rigorously computed positive natural density is a motivated nontrivial partial solution; the local obstructions at 2 and 3 and exact Euler product quantify how often this structured construction works. It does not assert the universal question is settled, nor merely recompute the source’s b<=10 table.
